scope: World asset files, registered model builders, exported scenery builders, resident cast and current Studio locations. Source references are evidence, not a runtime placement census. Instances, inline geometry and generated audio still need adapters.

purpose.who: Mrs Sato, serving coffee and cold barley tea.
purpose.why: Supports the coffee urn, jug and cups at working height instead of leaving them in mid-air.
purpose.where: At the east end of the ramen kitchen beside the serving pass.

purpose.who: The quay crew before and after a shift, the children on the Halloween walk, and anyone on Sakura Street who wants a cold sanpin tea or a hot J-Coffee.
purpose.why: Sixteen columns of the island’s own drinks, cold and hot, day and night: Minato Drinks fills it from its van every morning, and Sakura gives it the wall and the power for a share.
purpose.where: Against Sakura Shōten’s wall on Sakura Street, on its own concrete pad beside its own outdoor socket (okinawa/old-town.js SAKURA_VENDING).

purpose.who: The children on the Halloween walk along Sakura Street, and the shopkeepers who string the route for them.
purpose.why: Thirteen paper lanterns, a 25 W bulb in each, light the walk’s route on the last evening of October.
purpose.where: On one string from the nobori pole by the drinks machine, along the front edge of Sakura Shōten’s awning (halloween.js).

purpose.who: The children collecting sweets on the Halloween walk, who carry the pails from shop to shop.
purpose.why: A sweets pail lit inside by a little torch, so it glows in the walk’s photograph.
purpose.where: Ringed round Sakura’s drinks machine for the walk’s photograph (halloween.js, the story things).

purpose.who: The children on the Halloween walk, and the story’s séance, where one peeks from the crates.
purpose.why: A soft toy ghost, round and smiling: a Japanese Halloween’s obake is cute, not frightening.
purpose.where: Peeking from the crates beside Sakura’s drinks machine (halloween.js, the story things).

purpose.who: The children on the Halloween walk, at whose eye height the ghosts are taped.
purpose.why: Paper ghosts turn Sakura’s closed shutter into part of the walk.
purpose.where: Four of them taped to Sakura Shōten’s shutter at a child’s eye height (halloween.js).

purpose.who: The Tamashiro family, whose black dog he is, and the stories that need a dog on the street.
purpose.why: He barks at the postman’s Super Cub and nothing else; a dog makes a street lived in.
purpose.where: On Sakura Street with the Tamashiros on the Halloween evening (halloween.js, stage dog).

purpose.who: Kōji, who brought it from his boat shed, and Tetsuo, the electrician who finds the fault in it.
purpose.why: Thirty metres of thin cord still half coiled on its drum: the story’s trouble, carrying the machine’s start surge and the lanterns at once.
purpose.where: On the pavement by Sakura’s drinks machine and its outdoor socket (halloween.js, the reel).

purpose.who: The quay crew, who press it before and after a shift, and anyone at a drinks machine at night.
purpose.why: The island’s own canned black coffee (Minato Drinks, a made-up brand), ¥120 from the town’s machines; it sells out first at night.
purpose.where: Three columns of the bottom row of Sakura’s drinks machine, at hand height under the coin slot (vending.js VENDING_COLUMNS).

purpose.who: Tetsuo, who carries it in the stories.
purpose.why: The island’s electrician carries a pocket torch for dark switchboards and roof spaces; in Umi-no-yu’s blackout it is the only light, and he switches the loads off by it before the breaker goes back up.
purpose.where: Head down in his shirt pocket at the left chest beside his badge (after the bath, clipped to the vest’s neckline), where his right hand finds it without looking.

purpose.who: The bathers in Umi-no-yu’s changing rooms, and Thuan, who ends up wearing one in the blackout.
purpose.why: A rattan clothes basket at every locker: your clothes wait in it while you bathe.
purpose.where: On the locker shelves of Umi-no-yu’s changing rooms, the men’s side’s size, 0.40 × 0.40 × 0.22 m (story-props.js BASKET).

purpose.who: Tetsuo, who carries it in the stories.
purpose.why: After his bath he reads the evening paper on the koagari edge, which is why nobody pays him any attention until the lights go.
purpose.where: Folded once down the middle and held open like a book in both mittens, at reading distance before the chest.

purpose.who: Miss Higa, who carries it in the stories.
purpose.why: Between customers at the bandai she reads: a paperback novel from Front-Row Books & Stationery’s reading copies, a 1990s edition with its paper band (obi) still on, which is why she never looks up from it.
purpose.where: Held open in her right mitten at reading distance, the mitten under the foot of the spine, the pages turned up to her eyes and the cover with its band to the room.

purpose.who: Tetsuo, who carries it in the stories.
purpose.why: Prove dead before touching: a two-pole voltage tester, both probes on the terminals, a row of lamps for the voltage. He proves it on something live first, then the dead board, then live again (live, dead, live), so a broken tester can never tell him a live board is dead.
purpose.where: The main handle in his right mitten, probe tip out past his fingers; the second probe on its lead, parked on the handle until he takes it in his left mitten (testerSplit).

purpose.who: People walking up to Minato Park, who stop for a cup of sencha and a sata andagi.
purpose.why: A long bench in red felt under a paper parasol: somewhere to sit a while with tea and the view of the town.
purpose.where: On the open turf south of the path into Minato Park (park.js placeTeaStop), facing the path.

purpose.who: The residents who ride to the shops and the quay, and the player, who rides the bookshop’s one.
purpose.why: The island’s everyday transport: a commuter bicycle with a front basket, a rear carrier and a stand.
purpose.where: Parked outside Front-Row Books & Stationery (bicycle.js BOOKSHOP_BICYCLE) and along the harbour (harbour.js).

purpose.who: The izakaya’s regulars, and the player, whose own bottle waits on the keep shelf.
purpose.why: Bottle keep: you buy a whole bottle and Minato keeps it for you, with your name on its card, until your next visit.
purpose.where: On Minato’s keep shelf by the counter (izakaya-dressing.js KEEP_SHELF).

purpose.why: A cup of tea and the evening paper within reach of the cushion.
Clothes and papers in a chest of drawers, the way island homes kept them.
Paperbacks and sea charts at reading height from the floor.
Soft paper light on the floor for evenings without the ceiling lamp.
Something green and alive in the room; an areca palm likes the island light.
A zabuton for a guest, so nobody sits on the bare tatami.
A Swedish rag rug, woven from old shirts; a little of home on the tatami.
Somewhere to sit for people waiting, resting or watching the harbour; older residents walk further when there is a bench on the way.
purpose.where: pavement, park, quay

purpose.why: Letters and postcards; residents post on their way to work, so it belongs on a walking route.
purpose.where: pavement

purpose.why: Town news, lost cats and events; people stop and read, which starts conversations.
purpose.where: pavement, square

purpose.why: The morning paper for commuters, next to the shop that sells it.
purpose.where: pavement by a shop

purpose.why: Parking for people who cycle to the shops or the ferry.
purpose.where: pavement, station

purpose.why: Tonight's dishes, set out by the restaurant's door to bring people in.
purpose.where: outside a restaurant

purpose.why: Deliveries waiting to be unpacked; they show that a shop is supplied from somewhere.
purpose.where: yard, quay, back door

purpose.why: The street's electrics and phone lines; one stands near every block it serves.
purpose.where: pavement edge

purpose.why: Lets drivers and cyclists see round a corner they cannot see past.
purpose.where: a blind corner

purpose.why: Bait and ice for the people who fish from the pier.
purpose.where: quay

purpose.why: Hauls boats and heavy loads up from the water.
purpose.where: quay, pier

purpose.who: Islanders who work bare-headed under the Okinawan sun on the quay and the boats and want a good cap, not a giveaway: Kōji at the catch tables first, Riku on the cargo quay, Mr Fujita at the bow bollards.
purpose.why: A peak against the glare off the water, a mesh back that lets the sea wind through, a strap that fits anyone; made as well as an imported cap, by the town's own maker, with Johansson's J raised on the front.
purpose.where: On the cap tree at Sakura Shōten by the east window, beside the till and in the window, a stack on each cap form; and on the heads of whoever bought one (src/avatars/hat-assets.js fits it to any head).

purpose.who: Customers at Sakura Shōten looking at Johansson's trucker caps on the cap tree by the east window, before they ask Thuan for one: the boats' crews, the catch sorters and the cargo quay.
purpose.why: Six caps stand on the stand at once; at the worn cap's detail they took Sakura over its phone budget, so the stand shows the same cap built for being looked at from the shop floor, under half the triangles.
purpose.where: On the two cap forms of Sakura's cap tree (src/world/interiors/sakura-cap-stand.js), stacked three to a form; never on a head, where the worn cap (johansson-trucker) goes.

purpose.who: Bathers resting after the bath in Umi-no-yu's lobby: the regulars cooling down in their after-bath clothes, and Mr Fujita, whose back is always stiff from the boat.
purpose.why: Ten minutes of kneading for a ¥100 coin after a 42-degree soak; a sentō's lobby kept one so the regulars stayed for a coffee milk and the night game.
purpose.where: In the Umi-no-yu lobby by the milk cooler, its back to the east wall on the men's side, facing the room: where the onsen's chair stands now (onsen.js).
